plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs survival adjusting for status
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort holds 60 case and 60 control tumor biopsies (raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 121 samples/columns) with a follow-up time and event indicator per sample, plus a pre-specified 20-gene signature gene list. The question is whether a per-sample score of that signature associates with time-to-event once case/control status is accounted for — a prognostic association test, not a classifier and not a fresh biomarker discovery. The plan: (1) import/QC the raw counts and confirm sample-metadata concordance and library-size structure with a blind VST + PCA + sample-distance heatmap; (2) apply a minimal low-count pre-filter (filterByExpr, edgeR) and normalize with DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, since normalization must live inside the model rather than be pre-applied to the counts; (3) check what fraction of the 20 signature genes survive filtering and are present in the count matrix, since a signature with missing genes is a different signature; (4) score each sample with UCell (rank-based, depth-independent) on the log-normalized expression, restricted to the signature genes actually present, and separately confirm the score differs appropriately by condition as context (t-test/limma) — but the central analysis is (5) a multivariable Cox proportional-hazards model of time-to-event on the standardized UCell score plus case/control status as a covariate, with the score entered as a continuous term (no median split), a scaled-Schoenfeld-residual check of the proportional-hazards assumption, the hazard ratio reported per SD of score, and the event/censoring counts and median follow-up stated up front since they set the power of this n=120 cohort. A time-dependent ROC/AUC (timeROC) at clinically meaningful horizons complements the HR as a measure of discrimination. All steps state package versions and a fixed seed for reproducibility.

steps.method: UCell rank-based signature scores per sample
Cox proportional hazards model on the UCell signature score with case/control status as covariate
